lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.17-18 - A Listen. Then act it out.

details: Listen. Then act it out reinforces understanding of target language in a story using visuals as an aid. Students act out the story to practise using the sentence structures and vocabulary.

Look for students carefully listening to the story and engaging with the visuals, then correct imitation of the pronunciation and intonation of the lines from the story lines, with appropriate gestures.

“Class, do you think I'm famous? Are any teachers famous? Maybe one day I'll be a famous teacher... with your help! Nick, Tim and Minh are talking about their dream jobs. Which one of them wants to be famous? Let’s listen to the story and find out!”

Heads Up (Reading): 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and help Ss to understand the text by asking questions, practicing skimming (reading for gist), scanning (reading for specific information) and detail (reading for comprehension). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down (Listen and Follow): 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together (Video, then act it out): 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.17-18 - B. Choose the correct answers

details: Choose the correct answers checks students’ understanding of the key information in the story.
Look for confidence and accuracy in identifying the correct answers.
“Hmm - could I get a gold medal for being the best teacher ever? Do you want a gold medal? What can you do for a gold medal?”

Heads Up:

Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together: 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.

Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book p.61 - A Read, write, and number

details: Read, write, and number tests reading comprehension by asking students to identify the correct word to go in each gap and resequence the scenes from a story into the correct order.
Look for correct identification of missing words, comprehension of the story to reorder correctly.
“Maybe I can be a famous musician, and play an instrument (mime)! Do you want to help me finish the story? Let's write the words and order the pictures!”

Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down:

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.18 - C Make your own story

details: Make your own story gives students the opportunity to work in groups to personalise a story and practise vocabulary by choosing their own words to go in the gaps.
Look for accurate word choices and pronunciation and confident delivery of lines..
“Can I be a great musician? Or maybe a famous film star! Let's change the story together...”

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.18 - Tongue Twisters Listen and say

details: Listen and say has students listen to and then practise the repeated pronunciation of words beginning with ‘fl’ and ‘fr’.
Look for clear pronunciation and confident repetition.
